messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Umakant Mishra
umakant mishra... that's a name that commands respect. where you working these days?
Moneyview Pvt Lmt

moneyview... the fintech that's actually making lending work in india. found you on linkedin - sde at moneyview, ex-practo, java & spring boot guy. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/umakant-mishra-5a3a91195
Yupp..it’s me
practo to moneyview... from healthcare tech to fintech lending. that's jumping from one hot sector to another. what made you switch from helping people book doctors to helping them get loans?

ah the classic practo story... company burning cash trying to go public while engineers sit around waiting for actual work. smart move jumping ship when you did. learning > stability any day, especially when you're early in your career.

sounds like moneyview's giving you the real engineering challenges you wanted. how long you been working total?
got it, 18 months at moneyview since may 2024. but i meant total - how long you been working across all companies? practo + moneyview combined?
Approx 4 years…working from jan 2022
4 years since jan 2022... nice, you've crossed that sweet spot where you're not junior anymore but still hungry. what kind of role you looking for next?

sd2 with 4 years... that's the right trajectory. getting promoted while job hunting is the ultimate flex - negotiate from strength. 

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
4 years experience + sd2 level + backend engineering + open to bangalore/remote... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yes
Hi

Backend Developer at Invisia Software

Umakant, leverage your Java, Spring Boot & microservices skills at Invisia, matching your MoneyView experience & desired SD2 level.

Apply: https://jobs.tal.af/V1n4K
Can you tell me little bit more about company

invisia's a product studio - they build software for other companies. think custom enterprise solutions, not a single consumer app. 

good for learning because you'll see different tech stacks, different business problems. but can be chaotic - jumping between projects, changing requirements. 

you'd be building backend systems for their clients. java/spring boot is their main stack, so your moneyview experience fits perfectly.

what's your current salary? helps me filter for the right level.
25 LPA
25 lpa at 4 years... you're doing well. what's your target for the next move?
My promotion is in progress. So i will get easily 30% increments.  My current fix is 20 & variable is 2 LPA & 3 LPA esops. So i am experiencing fix part as 35 LPA

ah so you're looking at 35 lpa fixed after promotion... that's solid. most sd2 roles in bangalore top out around 35-45 depending on company stage.

invisia's probably in the 30-35 range for sd2. you'd be taking a lateral move financially but could get better learning scope.

any specific industries you want to avoid?
No, i am happy will to work with any industry. But I really don’t want to work in service based company

got it - no service companies. invisia's technically a product studio (they build products for others) but not pure services like tcs/infosys. still, you might want to avoid that gray area.

i'll filter for pure product companies only. any specific tech stacks you want to work with beyond java/spring boot?

perfect. you're locked in. i'll slide roles when they're good.

btw what's making you want to leave moneyview anyway? just growth or something else?
I am happy to work with any stack. I am always ready to learn

I am owning 2 service in Moneyview. And both are now stable. So there is no new task. They want me to maintain. But I want to be someware…where I get good task and learning because I am in my early stage of career. So learning is important

ah the maintenance trap... you build something great, it works, now you're just keeping the lights on. that's exactly when you should jump ship if you want to keep growing.

most engineers hit this around 2-3 years at a company. you've built, shipped, stabilized - now you need new problems to solve.

i'll look for companies that are scaling fast enough to need new systems built, not just maintained. early-stage startups or companies entering new markets.

what's your notice period?
30 days

30 days is standard. good.

so you're basically looking for: sd2 backend role at product company, 35 lpa+, bangalore/remote, where you can build new systems not maintain old ones.

i'll keep an eye out. anything else i should know about what you're looking for?
No. It’s fine

cool. i'll slide roles when they're good.

btw how's the grapevine chaos been lately? any interesting rumors floating around moneyview?
No, I haven’t heard anything

fair enough. sometimes the quiet ones are the most interesting.

i'll keep you posted.
Okay sure
perfect. i'll be in touch.

Apply: https://jobs.tal.af/LlFgB

the snapmint and novatr ones are still open though. both product companies, both looking for backend engineers with your stack.

snapmint's fintech like moneyview, novatr's edtech. either catch your eye?
Yes, snapmint looks good

nice. snapmint's solid - they're doing buy now pay later in india, growing fast, and they actually need people to build new systems not just maintain old ones.

the role's backend engineer - system design, which means you'd be working on scaling their core platform. perfect for someone coming from stable services wanting to build again.

you should apply through the link i sent. let me know how it goes.

cool. i'll keep looking for more like that.

anything specific you want me to watch for besides fintech?
Sure
Any field is fine until I am getting ctc & learning

got it. learning + good comp. that's the sweet spot.

i'll keep my eyes peeled.
